title: The No-Hunger Games: How GLP-1 Medication Adoption Is Changing Consumer Food Demand
authors: Sylvia Hristakeva; Jura Liaukonyte; Leo Feler
eligible_reason: Staggered binary adoption with never-treated controls estimated by TWFE. Households adopt GLP-1 medications at household-specific months between January 2023 and July 2024 (2,602 adopters; adoption month assigned to the first month of the three-month survey interval, so multiple cohorts), and each adopter is paired 1:1 with a never-adopting household (nearest-neighbor without replacement, no weights). Equation 1 is a binned post-adoption TWFE (household FE + month FE, no controls, clustered by household) and Equation 2 is an unstacked event study with relative-time indicators l = -6..6. The authors also report Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess, Callaway-Sant'Anna, Gardner (did2s) and Sun-Abraham estimates (Web Appendix D.1). JUDGMENT CALL: the estimation sample is defined by 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching but the regression itself is an unweighted TWFE, so I treated the matched sample as a sample restriction rather than a 'matching-based DiD'; if the lead reads the protocol's matching exclusion strictly, the paper drops out entirely. Treatment switches off for 888 discontinuing households: per protocol, post-discontinuation months (the beta_3 bin) must be dropped in re-estimation.
design_notes: Equation 1: ln(spending+1)_it = b1*GLP1_it x months1-6_it + b2*GLP1_it x months7-12_it + b3*GLP1_it x postdiscontinuation_it + alpha_i + gamma_t + e_it; GLP1_it = 1 once household i has adopted by month t. Adoption month (month 0) excluded from estimation; months between last confirmed use and first confirmed non-use excluded. Reference category = pre-adoption months (and, implicitly, months >= 13 of continued use, which have no bin). Equation 2: sum_{l=-6}^{6} b_l D^l_it + alpha_i + gamma_t (omitted relative period not stated; month 0 excluded). Numerator household panel, monthly, July 2022-September 2024; 22,691 survey-consistent households, estimation sample 2,602 adopters + 2,602 matched nonadopters (matched on type-2 diabetes indicator, income >$125k, age <64, children, preadoption grocery spend per member, baseline Healthiness Index; Table 2 balance). N = 109,817 household-months for the full sample. Outcomes: ln(1+monthly grocery spending), ln(1+monthly grocery item count), ln(1+food-away-from-home spending), ln(1+category spending) for 40 categories. SEs clustered by household. Footnote 9 robustness adds matched-control 'post' indicators (Web Appendix Table D1 col 5). Web Appendix D.4.2: negative binomial, LPM, levels.
estimators_reported: TWFE static with binned post periods
adoption_cohort_notes: Adoption months run January 2023-July 2024, but survey reports timing in three-month windows and the earliest month is assigned, so there are roughly 6-7 distinct adoption months; exact count not stated. Figure 2 plots adopters over time.

data_availability_statement: Verbatim: 'The data that support the findings of this article are not available; however, code and disguised data are available in https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/SVWBNT.' Numerator household panel and proprietary GLP-1 survey provided under a research agreement with Cornell; coauthor Feler is Numerator's Chief Economist.
screener_notes: Eligible staggered design with modern-estimator robustness in the appendix, but the published estimates cannot be reproduced from the Dataverse package because only disguised data are deposited; author/Numerator outreach would be required. Two protocol issues to settle: (1) 1:1 nearest-neighbor matched sample (unweighted TWFE afterwards) treated here as a sample restriction, not matching-based DiD; (2) treatment switches off on discontinuation, so re-estimation must drop post-discontinuation months and decide how to handle months >= 13 of continued use (currently in the reference category). Software of the Dataverse code not stated in the text. Batch year is 2025; the print issue is 2026.
